title: Failure probability of sparse partial-cycle extensions
summary: Determine the probability that the sparse partial-cycle algorithm cannot extend an acyclic degree-$(d-1)$ structure at degree $d$.

formal_statement.body: In the source's sparse variant of Algorithm 2, restrict the algebraic normal form to at most $k$ terms of every degree. For each admissible order $n$, extension degree $d$, cap $k$, and attempt cutoff $b$ when imposed, determine exactly or asymptotically the probability that the algorithm fails to find a proper coefficient vector $\alpha_d$ extending an acyclic partial cycle structure $C^{[\le d-1]}$ to an acyclic $C^{[\le d]}$.

scope.domain: Randomized sparse partial-cycle extensions in de Bruijn sequence search
assumptions: Algorithm 2 uses the source's random-choice model
The characteristic function has at most $k$ terms of each degree
A proper $\alpha_d$ preserves acyclicity through degree $d$
The modified experiment may abandon a branch after $b$ unsuccessful attempts
scope.unresolved_remainder: No inspected later result gives a general exact probability, a nontrivial uniform bound, or a complete asymptotic law for this conditional sparse-extension failure event.

citations.label: Li--Lin, sparse partial-cycle extension failure
citations.locator: Section VII, sparse search-space analysis, journal p. 607

progress.summary: The source states that sparse term restrictions can make a degree extension fail and that the probability of this failure is unknown.
